documents.title: Primary care: fatigue
documents.text: 43-year-old with fatigue for a year. Drinks two beers on weekends. Exam unremarkable. TSH normal. Advised sleep hygiene.

documents.title: Rheumatology: hand pain
documents.text: Pain and swelling of the second and third knuckles of both hands. Rheumatoid factor and anti-CCP negative. X-ray shows hook-like osteophytes at the second and third metacarpophalangeal joints. Impression: osteoarthritis.

documents.title: Liver panel and ferritin
documents.text: ALT 68 U/L. Ferritin 1,150 ng/mL. Transferrin saturation not performed.

documents.title: Primary care: lab review
documents.text: Raised ferritin and ALT attributed to alcohol use and possible fatty liver. Advised to stop drinking. Recheck in one year.

documents.title: Endocrinology: new diabetes
documents.text: New diabetes, HbA1c 7.8%, with BMI 24. Low testosterone with reduced libido. Started metformin and testosterone replacement.

documents.title: Dermatology: skin darkening
documents.text: Generalized bronze-gray skin darkening without sun exposure change. No rash. Assessed as post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation.

documents.title: Repeat ferritin
documents.text: Ferritin 1,420 ng/mL. Patient reports no alcohol for three years. Transferrin saturation not performed.

documents.title: Cardiology: shortness of breath
documents.text: Exertional breathlessness. Echocardiogram shows mildly reduced ejection fraction of 48% with normal coronary CT. Cause of cardiomyopathy not determined.

documents.title: Abdominal ultrasound
documents.text: Liver mildly enlarged with coarse echotexture. No focal lesion. Spleen normal.

documents.title: Primary care: follow-up
documents.text: Ongoing fatigue, joint pain, diabetes, and heart failure symptoms. Ferritin remains high despite abstinence. Family history: a cousin had liver cirrhosis without alcohol use. Genetic testing has not been discussed.
